newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent stable, traders await NYMEX direction.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent stable, traders await NYMEX direction.

text.p: IPE Brent futures were five cents higher on the day by midsession but trade was choppy with the market lacking any clear direction, traders said.
By 1200 GMT, July Brent was up five cents at $17.75 a barrel.
"The market is looking oversold near-term. It's due to find some support from consolidation after the heavy downside," said Tony Machachek of Credit Lyonnais Rouse.
But traders said the market was quiet and with only weak support at $17.65, they would be looking to see how NYMEX reacted at its opening.
"People are looking to see what the (United) States are going to do but if they start selling, I think it'll get hammered," one trader said.
Gas oil, meanwhile, was also looking to build on support from the yearly continuation low at 159.50 and inch higher.
Traders said the June contract could move up to $163.25 a tonne in the afternoon session.
By 1200 the contract was at $161.25 off $3 a tonne.
